chunks: 4499 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who married a woman and found her to be qarnāʾ. He said: “This one does not conceive; she is to be returned to her family.”

I said: What if he had entered upon her? He said: “If he knew before having intercourse with her, then had intercourse with her, he has accepted her. But if he did not know about her until after he had intercourse with her, then afterward, if he wishes, he may keep her, and if he wishes, he may send her to her family; and she is entitled to whatever she took from him because of what he made lawful from her private part.”

key_terms.تُرَدُّ: She is returned, meaning sent back to her family due to the defect
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her
key_terms.رَضِيَ بِهَا: He accepted her condition and waived objection
key_terms.سَرَّحَهَا: He releases or sends her away to her family
key_terms.فَرْجِهَا: Her private part, referring here to lawful marital access
key_terms.قَرْنَاءَ: A woman described as having a genital obstruction or defect affecting intercourse and conception
key_terms.يُجَامِعَهَا: To have sexual intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband discovers a genital defect in his wife after marriage or after consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning marriage annulment when a woman is discovered to have a physical defect affecting marital relations and childbearing. It explains that prior knowledge followed by consummation counts as acceptance, while discovery after consummation leaves the husband with a choice, and the woman retains the dower in return for the lawful consummation.
